title: What a session said
description: GET /v1/transcript reads the assistant's own record and carries evidence rather than presenting content with no source. The initial request reads the newest page; before=nextBefore reads the next older page at a JSONL row boundary; after=nextAfter reads only the rows appended since, oldest first, and is refused 409 transcript_cursor_stale when the cursor no longer meets the record or the appended rows exceed one page (or, for Claude, hold a peer message), so the reader reads the newest page whole. Native Antigravity cursors require revision=signature from the exact held cursor page. A before read requires the current full snapshot revision; an after read verifies that the held revision is still the unchanged file prefix. Missing, replaced, truncated or edited revisions are refused as transcript_cursor_stale. Cloud carries before and revision but deliberately omits nextAfter and refuses after. Each page remains bounded by its row, byte and read-window limits.

TranscriptSplice.description: One replacement in the exact held page. Equal prefix and suffix entries are retained, including distinct repeated entries.

TranscriptDelta.description: Opt-in delta-v1 reply. Apply only to baseVersion of the exact pinned Session; replace metadata with page and apply ordered, non-overlapping splices in original base coordinates atomically. A cache miss or a larger delta returns a full TranscriptPage. Unchanged remains the existing version receipt.

entryCount.description: Exact resulting row count, including provider rows that expand into multiple entries.

TranscriptEntry.description: One thing in a conversation, in the shape the Swift app's `transcriptRows` writes it. A tool call and what the tool returned both carry `role: tool`; only the call names its tool. A call's `text` is the one line describing what it was asked to do — a command, a path, a query — which is what a folded row shows as its subject. An `AskUserQuestion` call carries its questions instead, after the U+0001 `ask` U+0001 marker.

artifacts.description: Pictures an assistant turn showed with a `<clawdline-image>` marker, or a Clawdline session message carried. Resolved against this daemon's store and then, read-only, the Swift app's.

at.description: Unix seconds. Absent when the record carried no timestamp this reader accepts.

fileChanges.description: Exact edits: a Codex patch, or the whole file a Claude `Write` created. Absent on every other entry.

imageCount.description: Images attached to a user turn. Absent when there were none: the Swift app writes an explicit 0 on user rows, and a reader treats absence as that 0.

id.description: Stable entry identity when the provider has a durable projection. Owned ACP uses acp2:generation:ordinal, preserving distinct repeated turns and replacing streamed content in place. Absent for providers without entry identities.

role.description: user, assistant, error (a provider failure that ended a turn), peer (another Claude Code session), message (another session through Clawdline), notice (Clawdline about a task) or tool.

source.description: The human-facing name of the session a peer or message row came from.

sourceAssistant.description: Which assistant sent a Clawdline session message.

sourceMode.description: How a peer or message row arrived: the peer's own mode, or `clawdline`.

tool.description: The tool a call used. Absent on a tool's result and on prose.

TranscriptEntryDetail.description: An opt-in stored tool body. The reference binds a native row, its full projected content, machine and Session execution. Body fields arrive only after expansion.

content.description: The whole file, for an addition, a deletion or a Claude `Write`.

kind.description: add, delete, update or write, as the record spelled it; `change` when it did not.

status.description: pending, inProgress or completed — Codex app-server's spelling, not the rollout's in_progress.

TranscriptActivity.description: What a Codex tool item recorded about itself: `called` for an MCP call with a title, `explored` for a shell command Codex classified as reads and searches.

agentID.description: Explicit native trajectory namespace for a tool from another agent; absent when its owner was not supplied.

toolCallID.description: Native tool identity, stable across partial updates.

resultKnown.description: True when a native result was received, including an explicitly empty result.

durationMs.description: How long the item took. -1 when the record did not say, which the Swift app sends as an absent key; 0 is a real, sub-millisecond duration and is drawn as one.

result.description: A called tool result. Owned ACP retains complete received text and pages large bodies on demand; older readers may provide a clipped result.

reference.description: Opaque stored row offset and content digest; only readable in the same Session execution.

toolID.description: Native tool call identity when the provider recorded one.

line.description: One-based first source line, when supplied.

endLine.description: Inclusive one-based last source line, when supplied.

TranscriptNotice.description: A decoded Clawdline notice without its protocol, version and body — the Swift app's `webObject`. Which fields are present depends on `kind`: task_finished, workspace_overlap, file_wait_request, file_wait_release or handoff_receipt.

leftovers.description: task_finished only: how many things the delivery said it left undone. Present only when above zero.

outstanding.description: task_finished only, where the decoder requires it, so absence there means 0.

TranscriptTruncation.description: The newest entries were kept and older ones left out, because the whole page would have passed its byte budget.

TranscriptUnread.description: This read looked at only the newest `windowBytes` of the record and ran out of them before it had as many entries as were asked for, so the conversation goes back further than the first entry here: `bytes` older bytes were not read at all. The Swift app cuts the same window and says nothing; this is the flag it lacks (docs/limits.md N17), so a page drawn from it can say that older content was not loaded instead of looking complete.

bytes.description: How many bytes before the window were not read. Always more than zero.

windowBytes.description: How much of the record's end one read looks at.

TranscriptPage.description: `entries`, `signature` and `truncation` are the Swift app's transcript payload; `evidence`, `path` and `note` say where the reading came from; `unread` is this daemon's own, and says the read window stopped short of the conversation's start.

leftovers.description: task_finished only: how many things the delivery said it left undone. Present only when above zero.

nextBefore.description: Exclusive provider cursor for the next older page: a JSONL byte offset or a durable owned ACP entry ordinal. Pass it back unchanged with this page's signature. Absent at the beginning of the record, and on an after= page.

readBefore.description: Optional exclusive opaque cursor for rereading this exact durable ACP page with its signature, including after its entries leave the newest window.

nextAfter.description: The byte offset just past the last complete row read: pass it as after= to read only what was appended since. Absent when nothing complete was read (no record yet, or an unreadable one), and from a daemon that does not take after=; a reader without it keeps reading the newest page whole.

path.description: Which file this was read from. A reading that cannot name its source is not evidence.

version.description: Digest of this exact compact page, scoped to machine and Session execution.

signature.description: Opaque record revision, empty when nothing was read. Claude/Codex use size and modification time; native Antigravity uses agy1:file-generation:prefix-bytes:sha256; durable owned ACP uses acp2:generation:revision, where only a native history replacement changes generation. Return this exact held page signature as revision with its before/after cursor; never substitute another page's signature.
